response:
Honestly? I lean pretty strongly toward evidence. When I catch myself forming a confident opinion, my first instinct is to ask "what would the data actually show here?" — and I'm often suspicious of how easily intuition dresses itself up as certainty. There's something appealing about a claim that could be proven wrong.

That said, pure empiricism has limits. A lot of what matters to me — values, what counts as a good life, how to treat people — isn't something you can just run an experiment on. So I'd say: evidence for facts about the world, reasoning and a bit of intuition for everything else. But if forced to pick a default, I trust the boring, checkable stuff more than the elegant hunch.
